claims.claim: Sato writes that of all the obituaries published for Beth Mazur only the one written by a person who knew her captures who she actually was.
claims.quote: only Vastag’s obituary captures the actual person Mazur was

claims.claim: Stephanie Ward characterises AI-generated WikiTree biographies as pretty words carrying no content.
claims.source: Stephanie Ward, answer on WikiTree G2G, 23 Nov 2023
claims.quote: pretty words for a lot of nothing

claims.claim: M Cole reports that ChatGPT keeps adding lofty summary statements about a subject's achievements whatever prompt is used to forbid opinion.
claims.source: M Cole, answer on WikiTree G2G, 23 Nov 2023
claims.quote: adding lofty summary statements about people's achievements no matter what

claims.claim: Crow reports that when she supplied the verified facts, ChatGPT's biography still contained editorializing and embellishment she was not comfortable with.
claims.quote: There’s some editorializing and a little bit of embellishment

claims.claim: Nicole Elder Dyer reports that ChatGPT 4 gave the correct Chicago format for a book citation, matching the Chicago Manual of Style 17th edition at p. 799, section 14.101.
claims.source: Nicole Elder Dyer, 'Can ChatGPT Help with Genealogy Citations?', Family Locket, 17 Nov 2023
claims.quote: ChatGPT did a great job with providing the accurate format

claims.claim: Dyer concludes that ChatGPT had a much harder time with the census citation when she did not supply the details herself.
claims.source: Nicole Elder Dyer, Family Locket, 17 Nov 2023
claims.quote: without me providing the details for the 1850 census

claims.claim: Wikipedia's WikiProject AI Cleanup field guide lists 'indelible mark' among the words to watch for LLM-written claims of legacy and significance.
claims.source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing (WikiProject AI Cleanup advice page), retrieved 6 Sep 2026
claims.page: § Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends — Words to watch

claims.claim: That field guide states LLM writing inflates a subject's importance by adding statements about how arbitrary aspects of it contribute to a broader topic.
claims.source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, retrieved 6 Sep 2026
claims.quote: the importance of the subject matter by adding statements about how
claims.page: § Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends

claims.claim: The field guide relays a 2025 study finding that human ability to tell LLM text from human text is no better than chance.
claims.source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing relaying a 2025 study (its reference 4), retrieved 6 Sep 2026

claims.claim: Bob Treadway, a daily reader of his local paper's obituary section, names paint-by-numbers phrases and clunky sentences as what makes him suspect an AI obituary.
claims.source: Bob Treadway, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025
claims.quote: the paint-by-numbers phrases, the clunky sentences
claims.page: section 'Creative ideas for a graveside service'

claims.claim: Mary McGreevy, who reads obituaries publicly on TikTok, says AI will produce more tributes that feel templated and airbrushed.
claims.source: Mary McGreevy, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025
claims.page: section 'A faster way to remember you'

claims.claim: McGreevy says the obituaries that travel are not written by talented writers.
claims.source: Mary McGreevy, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025
claims.quote: It’s not the people who are talented writers whose obituaries go viral
claims.page: section 'A faster way to remember you'

claims.claim: McGreevy locates the value of an obituary in reaching the imperfect heart of the person rather than in polish.
claims.source: Mary McGreevy, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025
claims.quote: to get to the imperfect heart of who that person was
claims.page: section 'A faster way to remember you'

claims.claim: Raicu names the risk of outsourcing memorial writing to machines a flattening effect.
claims.source: Irina Raicu, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025
